name: Range slider
purpose: Lets a user select a MIN/MAX pair along a bounded numerical scale using two independent handles — e.g. 'Price range: £200–£800'. Itinerary row 24 (P3, 'Dual-handle'), explicitly mapped to NOT be the gated single-thumb Slider (Slider.reference.html), which this component ACCRETES from rather than re-draws.
$status: PROPOSED #209, Dave's eye owed — new component, built through the gated-component route at #209 wave 3 lane B. Nothing about it is ruled.
$accretesFrom: knowledge/snippets/Slider.reference.html (gated). Copied verbatim: the linear-gradient track-fill technique driven by a CSS custom property, the 20px/2px-border thumb geometry, the focus-ring-on-thumb treatment, the 'value also shown as text, never colour/position alone' answer to 1.4.1, and the reduced-motion collapse. The ONLY authored addition is the SECOND handle and its consequences (see behaviour.$authored below) — there is no single-handle precedent for a two-input clamp or z-index handoff.

props.name: valueLow
props.$note: The low handle's current value. Clamped so it can never exceed valueHigh (authored JS, see behaviour).

props.name: valueHigh
props.$note: The high handle's current value. Clamped so it can never fall below valueLow.

props.name: unit
props.$note: Prefix/suffix for the displayed value pair, e.g. '£'. Specimen shows GBP; not itself a currency-formatting component.

props.name: disabled
props.$note: NOT DRAWN as a specimen this pass — the gated Slider has no disabled specimen either; carried as a declared gap, not invented here to avoid drifting ahead of its own precedent.

variants.name: default
variants.use: Two handles, a filled band between them, min/max value pair shown as text.

tokens.track-filled: scrollbar/foreground — the filled BAND between the two handles, copied from Slider's single-stop gradient technique, extended to a two-stop band
tokens.track-unfilled: scrollbar/background — the two OUTER segments (below the low handle, above the high handle)
tokens.handle: tertiary/background/default + form/border/default border — REBOUND from Slider's own background/default + border/subtle for the same reason Slider's meta already records (invisible-in-dark finding, see $differsFrom)
tokens.value-label: text/default @ .t-cm-label (field label) / .t-cm-figure-6 (the £lo–£hi value pair, tabular figures)
tokens.focus: focus/ring — 2px outline, offset 2, on whichever thumb has DOM focus
tokens.$note: NO NEW TOKEN IS WANTED OR MINTED. Every value already exists and is already bound by the gated Slider or List-items' amount figure.

motion.reducedMotion: Global prefers-reduced-motion collapse present, copied from Slider.

responsive.rule: The field is max-width:360px and the rail is width:100% inside it — reflows naturally in a form column down to narrow viewports; no breakpoint-specific behaviour was needed or added.

accessibility.role: Two real <input type="range"> elements, each with its own aria-labelledby (sharing the field's one visible label) and a live aria-valuetext ('£200, minimum' / '£800, maximum') so AT never has to infer which handle is which from position alone.
accessibility.keyboard: Native — Arrow keys/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown operate whichever handle has focus, exactly as the gated Slider's single handle does. No custom keydown handler was authored; the browser's own range-input keyboard model is reused twice.
accessibility.valueText: aria-valuetext is recomputed on every input event for BOTH handles (the low handle's text also changes near the clamp boundary), and the visible value pair mirrors it as plain text — never colour or handle position alone (1.4.1), the same answer the gated Slider gives.
accessibility.targetArea: Handle hit target min 44px even though the visual thumb is 20px — copied from Slider's own antiPattern guard.
accessibility.clamp: The low handle cannot be dragged/keyed past the high handle and vice versa (authored JS). The clamp is silent (no error message) — DECIDED here as a UX default, not settled: should crossing produce a message, or is silent clamping sufficient? See $decisionsForDave.

antiPatterns: Handle hit target smaller than 44px (carried from Slider)
No keyboard operation for either handle (carried from Slider)
Letting the low handle's DOM z-index get permanently trapped under the high handle at a shared value — the is-top class swap on pointerdown exists specifically to prevent this

Synthesising a single custom control with two drawn thumbs instead of two real range inputs — the two-native-inputs technique is what earns the keyboard model honestly, at the cost of the clamp needing to be authored

tokenValidation.against: knowledge/tokens/semantic-colour.json via #token-manifest (mono values only — REBIND SOURCE, see $note)

tokenValidation.$note: Every var name and mono value was copied byte-for-byte from Slider.reference.html except --handle/--handle-bd, which this component instead points at tertiary/background/default + form/border/default (Slider's OWN meta already records background/default+border/subtle as invisible in dark — this snippet starts from the already-fixed pair rather than re-introducing the bug). Four-theme legs NOT independently re-measured this pass (declared, not run — see receipt).

provenance.$note: Itinerary row 24 (reviews/ITINERARY-STATUS-2026-08-19-v1.json), measured a TRUE GAP: all five signal probes negative on range-slider, drift AGREES. Explicitly NOT row 12/Slider — the itinerary's own 'why' field flags the fuzzy-match risk.

$differsFrom.Slider: Slider is single OR double per its own 'type' enum/variant — but its double variant is documented as two handles on ONE input's worth of markup in the Figma source (see slider.meta.json variants.double), not built out as a live gated snippet. This component is the ACTUAL two-native-input implementation the itinerary's row 24 asks for, sharing every visual/token idiom with Slider but adding the real dual-handle mechanics (clamp, two aria-valuetext channels, z-index handoff) that a Figma variant name alone does not supply.

$decisionsForDave: Should crossing the clamp boundary produce a message (e.g. a brief inline note) or stay a silent clamp, as built?
Slider's own meta records a DEPRECATED tick-marker token finding — should Range slider inherit tick markers at all, or stay bare (as built)?
Is £/GBP the right specimen currency, or should the canonical specimen be currency-neutral (a plain numeric range) with money shown only in a usage example?
